title: Latency Horizon: model-route latency synthesis with streaming vs blocking breakdown
creator: Leah Kim
description:
Goal: Build a concise, production-ready dashboard that synthesizes end-to-end latency by model and API route with an explicit split between streaming and non-streaming (blocking) requests. This ticket covers: (1) tracing/span tag standardization for io_mode, model_family, model_version, route, and batch_size; (2) metrics pipeline definition (histogram buckets, percentiles) and mapping to our analytics backend; (3) dashboard panels and alerts for p50/p95/p99 by model-route-io_mode cohorts; (4) drilldowns for tail traces and error correlation.

Background: We have many ad-hoc dashboards showing latency percentiles but inconsistent tagging (sometimes "stream" vs "nonstream" vs absent). That prevents reliable aggregation across deployments and confuses SLA calculation for Dedicated customers. This work should make latencies comparable across hosted/dedicated/private environments by enforcing a small set of canonical fields on traces and metrics and by providing a single dashboard that product, SRE, and solutions engineers can use for incident triage and capacity planning.

Scope:
- Instrument tracing hooks to add/normalize span attributes: io_mode = {"streaming","blocking"}, model_family, model_variant, route, request_shape_bucket (short/medium/long), kv_cache_hit = {"yes","no"}.
- Emit a latency histogram metric (ms) at the serving ingress and at the final response codeline to allow compute of service-only vs e2e latency.
- Ingest histograms into the metrics pipeline with the following percentile rollups: p50, p95, p99 and a tail-sample collector for p999 sampling.
- Dashboard panels: per-model-family grid with selectable route, stacked comparison streaming vs blocking, cohort selector for request_shape, and heatmap of percentiles over time.
- Alerts: create a baseline SLO comparison panel and a firing rule prototype (e.g., p95 > 250ms for 5m for any model-route with >1000 requests/min).

Success criteria:
- All requests include canonical span attributes in 95% of production requests within 2 weeks of rollout.
- A single dashboard view exists that shows p50/p95/p99 by model and route with an explicit toggle for io_mode and that is usable for first responder triage.
- On-call runbook updated with how to use the dashboard and how to pivot to traces for root cause.

Data sources and queries (examples):
- Traces: OpenTelemetry spans exported to our tracing backend. Required attributes: service.name, span.duration_ms, io_mode, model_family, route, request_shape_bucket, kv_cache_hit, host_region.
- Metrics ingestion: histogram metric name: redwood.serve.latency_ms -> buckets [1,5,10,25,50,100,200,400,800,1600,3200].
- Example aggregation (promql-like pseudo): quantile_over_time(0.95, histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_serve_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, model_family, route, io_mode))).
- Tail sampling: on p99+ triggers, emit trace id to a tail archive index (for later batch analysis).

UI notes: dashboard should be compact for paging through model families, have deep-linking to a trace explorer with prefilled filters, and a CSV export of percentile time-series for postmortem analysis.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement tracing hook changes behind a feature flag (serving runtime + gateway).
2) Add histogram emission to metricsers behind same flag.
3) Turn on ingestion in staging and validate percentiles against synthetic traffic.
4) Gradual production rollout by region and model-family; monitor canonical attribute presence metric.

Privacy & compliance: ensure model identifiers are stable but do not expose customer prompts or PII in span attributes. Use hashed route IDs where routes are customer-specific.
acceptance_criteria: Tracing hooks add canonical span attributes for io_mode, model_family, model_variant, route, request_shape_bucket in 95% of sampled traces
Histogram metrics present in metrics backend and panel renders p50/p95/p99 for selected model-route-io_mode
Dashboard includes streaming vs blocking visual split and deep-links into trace explorer
Runbook updated with usages and at least one on-call walk-through completed
